module purpose: neorv32_dmem implements an internal 32-bit data memory behind a request/response bus record interface. It writes addressed byte lanes of the request data into four RAM byte arrays, loads the addressed read word into rdata, returns it on read requests, acknowledges each strobe, and ties the error response low.

use-case flows.value: addressed byte-lane writes from the request data into the internal memory arrays
addressed memory word loaded from the RAM arrays and made available for read responses
acknowledge response following the request strobe
rden and acknowledge cleared when rstn_i is low

conceptual assets.reasoning: Lines 61-73 write request-data byte lanes into mem_ram_b0..b3 at `to_integer(addr)` when `bus_req_i.stb`, `bus_req_i.rw` and the corresponding `bus_req_i.ben` bit qualify the store, and lines 75-78 later read those same arrays. Integrity of the memory operation requires the stored bytes to remain correct for later addressed reads; availability is established because these arrays are the only state holding DMEM contents between accesses. `alt_style_c` is constant false (line 36), so the reachable write points are lines 63, 66, 69 and 72.

Lines 75-78 load `rdata` from the four RAM byte arrays at the selected `addr`, and line 129 uses `rdata` as the source of the response data when `rden = '1'`. Integrity requires the read-out word to equal the addressed stored word; availability is established for read cycles because line 124 captures the read request into `rden`. Although the map lists `addr_ff`-based assignments, `alt_style_c` is constant false (line 36), so lines 75-78 are the active read-data assignments.

`addr <= unsigned(bus_req_i.addr(addr_hi_c downto 2));` (line 113) computes the internal word index, and that index is used in every active write `to_integer(addr)` (lines 63, 66, 69, 72) and active read (lines 75-78). Integrity of both the write and read-out flows requires the selected memory word to match this index; availability of access to the intended word also depends on it. The `addr_ff` path belongs only to the unreachable `alt_style_c` branch.

Line 124 registers `rden` as `bus_req_i.stb and (not bus_req_i.rw)`, and line 129 uses `rden` to choose between `rdata` and zero on the response-data path. Integrity requires this decision to qualify only reads, and availability of read data under that RTL-visible condition depends on it.

Lines 120-125 define the acknowledge event: reset forces `bus_rsp_o.ack` low at line 122, and line 125 copies the sampled strobe into the response acknowledge. Integrity requires the reported handshake to match the request strobe, and availability requires it to be produced on clocked cycles with `rstn_i = '1'`. No eligible structural reference survives because the only declaration realizing it is the `ack` field of the transport response port `bus_rsp_o`, and transport ports are excluded.
